findings.title: Missing cache re-check after acquiring write lock causes redundant manifest reads
findings.body: GetWebAssets snapshots the cache under RLock (line 41-43), and if it is nil acquires the exclusive Lock (line 48) but never re-checks entryPointAssetsCache after taking the lock. When the cache is cold (e.g. at startup) or always in Dev mode, every goroutine that saw nil in the read-lock phase queues on the write lock and each one independently performs the manifest file read/JSON decode (and, in Dev, potentially the CDN fetch) while holding the exclusive lock. The result is serialized, repeated I/O for N concurrent requests instead of a single load, and each late arrival overwrites the cache written by the previous one. A double-checked-locking pattern (re-test `cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil` immediately after `Lock()` and return the cached value) is needed to avoid the thundering-herd recompute.

findings.title: No test verifying the race fix
findings.body: The PR claims to fix a data race on the shared entryPointAssetsCache global, but no test is added that exercises GetWebAssets concurrently (e.g. many goroutines calling it in non-Dev mode with a fixed manifest) and run under `-race`. Without such a test, a future refactor that drops or narrows the locking would silently reintroduce the race without CI detecting it. A concurrency test should be added to lock in the fix.
